question: I need to repair a loose floor joist in my backyard shed, but the joist is 12 feet long and I don't have any help to lift it into place. What should I do?
answer: To secure a long floor joist without a partner, you'll need to use a combination of techniques and equipment. First, prepare the joist by drilling a series of evenly spaced holes along its length, about 6 inches apart. Next, use a piece of 2x4 lumber and some 3-inch screws to create a makeshift 'joist dolly' - this will allow you to support the joist while you move it into place. Once you have the dolly in place, use a hand saw or a reciprocating saw to carefully cut the joist to a length that can be easily handled by one person. Finally, use some clamps and some wood glue to secure the joist in place. Be careful not to damage the surrounding structure or the joist itself, as this can lead to further instability and potentially catastrophic failure. Specifically, be aware of the risk of the joist slipping out of the dolly and causing injury, so take care to secure it firmly before starting to move it. To mitigate this risk, make sure to use a stable and level surface for the dolly, and consider enlisting a second person to hold the dolly in place while you cut the joist to length.
equipment_problem: securing a long floor joist without a partner
steps: Drill holes along the length of the joist, about 6 inches apart
Create a makeshift joist dolly using a 2x4 and some 3-inch screws
Cut the joist to a length that can be easily handled by one person
Use clamps and wood glue to secure the joist in place
